claim_text: Tomingley employs a range of measures to optimise water management and minimise consumption of clean (raw) water.
metric_name: Bore water use per tonne of ore processed; bore water use per ounce of gold poured
context_text:
For example, surface runoff due
to rainfall is contained in sediment ponds, then used
for dust suppression. The process water system
preferentially uses water from an internal recycling
circuit, with new bore water used to top up the
process water only as required. Water is recovered
and recycled multiple times before it evaporates out
of the process water system
[table]Tomingley bore water use consumption and efficiency
Per tonne of ore processed (L/t) FY2024 415  FY2025 411
Per ounce of gold poured (L/oz) FY2024 8214 FY2025 6804
label: Partially Supported
rationale_short: The report clearly supports that Tomingley uses multiple water-management measures, and the efficiency metrics improved year on year, but the evidence is not strong enough to fully substantiate the stronger wording 'minimise consumption'.
llm_reason: The claim’s central assertion is that Tomingley uses multiple measures to optimise water management and minimise consumption of clean (raw) water. The evidence substantiates this by describing specific practices that reduce raw bore water demand: capturing rainfall runoff in sediment ponds for dust suppression; preferentially using an internal recycling circuit for process water; using new bore water only to top up process water as required; and recovering/recycling water multiple times before it evaporates. The evidence also provides bore water consumption efficiency metrics showing bore water use per tonne of ore processed decreased from 415 L/t (FY2024) to 411 L/t (FY2025) and bore water use per ounce of gold poured decreased from 8214 L/oz (FY2024) to 6804 L/oz (FY2025), consistent with minimising raw water consumption.
